title: HiFi-DRAM: Enabling High-fidelity DRAM Research by Uncovering Sense Amplifiers with IC Imaging
problem: DRAM vendors do not disclose the architecture of sense amplifiers in their chips, forcing researchers to rely on assumptions without knowing circuit topology, transistor dimensions, or layouts. This information gap severely impairs the fidelity of DRAM studies and causes research to be based on inaccurate models.
motivation: Accurate knowledge of actual DRAM sense amplifier designs is essential for academic researchers to model and improve modern DRAM systems with high fidelity.
method: The authors use specialized microscopes—scanning electron microscopes (SEM) to take extremely detailed pictures and focused ion beams (FIB) to carefully slice through chips—to look inside the sense amplifiers in actual DDR4 and DDR5 chips from three major vendors. They physically prepare samples, photograph the internal circuits at nanometer scales, and measure actual transistor sizes and layouts. The imaging revealed that real DRAM sense amplifiers use offset-cancellation designs (circuits that actively cancel out error signals) rather than the simpler designs researchers had assumed, and the transistors are sized differently than literature predictions.
key_novelty: They were the first to physically photograph the inside of real DRAM chips using electron microscopes and ion beams to reveal exactly how the sense amplifiers (the read circuits) are designed and built—details that manufacturers had kept secret.
contributions: Reverse-engineered circuit topologies and physical layouts of sense amplifiers in DDR4/DDR5 from major vendors
Discovered that offset-cancellation designs replace classical sense amplifier topologies in modern DRAM
Measured actual transistor dimensions, showing up to 9x inaccuracy in public DRAM models
Open-sourced reverse-engineered circuits and layouts to enable high-fidelity future DRAM research

metrics.other: up to 9x inaccuracy in public DRAM models; up to 175x error in research estimations of proposed changes

primary_theme: reverse-engineering DRAM sense amplifiers via IC imaging
